ambiguities.text: The EIP does not specify if MAX_PER_EPOCH_ACTIVATION_CHURN_LIMIT can be adjusted in future upgrades without breaking existing validator expectations.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the constant is a protocol parameter that can be modified via hard fork, similar to other consensus constants.

ambiguities.text: The EIP describes this as 'a temporary measure while the community develops more comprehensive solutions' without defining success criteria or timeline.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this limit remains in effect until explicitly superseded by another EIP addressing reward curves or staking economics.

implicit_assumptions.description: The asymmetry between bounded entry and unbounded exit queues will not cause significant validator set instability.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Mass exit events could rapidly decrease validator count, potentially affecting finality or enabling attacks requiring low validator participation.

implicit_assumptions.description: The deposit queue will remain at or near capacity, making the churn limit the binding constraint.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If staking demand decreases below the churn limit, this EIP has no practical effect on growth rate.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot exploit the asymmetric entry/exit to manipulate the validator set composition.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Potential for validator set manipulation by coordinating large exits followed by strategic re-entries.
